TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT

ARTIFACTS_FILE="$TMP_DIR/artifacts.jsonl"
: > "$ARTIFACTS_FILE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# sha256 of file content (empty string if unreadable)
file_sha256() {
    sha256sum -- "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'
}

# first 100 chars of a string, newlines turned into \n literals
preview_of() {
    local s="$1"
    s="${s:0:100}"
    s="${s//$'\n'/\\n}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

# record one artifact (type, path, sha256, line_number, content_preview, user)
add_artifact() {
    local type="$1" path="$2" sha="$3" lineno="$4" preview="$5" user="$6"
    jq -cn \
        --arg type "$type" \
        --arg path "$path" \
        --arg sha "$sha" \
        --argjson lineno "$lineno" \
        --arg preview "$preview" \
        --arg user "$user" \
        '{type: $type, path: $path, sha256: $sha,
          details: {line_number: $lineno, content_preview: $preview, user: $user}}' \
        >> "$ARTIFACTS_FILE" 2>/dev/null
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cron detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Is the command a standard system command (not a script outside standard paths)?
is_standard_command() {
    local cmd="$1"
    # absolute path inside a standard system directory
    case "$cmd" in
        /bin/*|/usr/bin/*|/sbin/*|/usr/sbin/*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    # well-known benign command names
    case "$cmd" in
        test*|cd*|run-parts*|env*|true|true*|false|false*|sleep*|sh*|bash*|/bin/sh*|/bin/bash*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

# Obfuscation / payload indicators present in a command
has_obfuscation() {
    local cmd="$1"
    case "$cmd" in
        */tmp*|*/var/tmp*|*/dev/shm*) return 0 ;;
        *base64*|*eval*|*eval\ *|*wget*|*curl*) return 0 ;;
        *\.sh*|*\.py*|*\.pl*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

# Unusual timing pattern: every minute or every few minutes/hours
is_unusual_timing() {
    local f1="$1" f2="$2" f3="$3" f4="$4" f5="$5"
    local field
    for field in "$f1" "$f2" "$f3" "$f4" "$f5"; do
        case "$field" in
            *|*/1|*/2|*/3|*/4|*/5|0/1|0/2) : ;;
            *) return 1 ;;
        esac
    done
    return 0
}

# scan one cron file: $1 = path, $2 = "6" (has user field) or "5" (user crontab)
scan_cron_file() {
    local file="$1" has_user="$2"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local sha line cmd user lineno
    sha="$(file_sha256 "$file")"
    [ -n "$sha" ] || return 0
    lineno=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        # strip leading whitespace
        local t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        # skip blank lines and comments
        [ -z "$t" ] && continue
        case "$t" in \#*) continue ;; esac
        # variable assignments (SHELL=, PATH=, ...)
        case "$t" in *=*) case "$t" in [A-Za-z_]*=*) continue ;; esac ;; esac

            local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
            user="null"

                user="${rest%%[[:space:]]*}"
                cmd="${rest#* }"
            else
                cmd="$rest"
            fi
        elif [[ "$t" =~ ^([0-9*,/-]+)[[:space:]]+([0-9*,/-]+)[[:space:]]+([0-9*,/-]+)[[:space:]]+([0-9*,/-]+)[[:space:]]+([0-9*,/-]+)[[:space:]]+(.+)$ ]]; then
            local f1="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" f2="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}" f3="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
            local f4="${BASH_REMATCH[4]}" f5="${BASH_REMATCH[5]}"
            local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[6]}"
            user="null"
            if [ "$has_user" = "6" ]; then
                user="${rest%%[[:space:]]*}"
                cmd="${rest#* }"
            else
                cmd="$rest"
            fi

                add_artifact "cron_job" "$file" "$sha" "$lineno" \
                    "$(preview_of "$line")" "$user"
                continue

            continue   # not a recognizable cron entry
        fi

        cmd="${cmd%%#*}"
        cmd="$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//')"

            suspicious=1

        fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Systemd unit detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

declare -A SEEN_UNITS=()

scan_systemd_file() {
    local file="$1"
    [ -e "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local real
    real="$(readlink -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || real="$file"
    [ -f "$real" ] || return 0
    # report the actual (resolved) file path; deduplicate resolved paths
    if [ -n "${SEEN_UNITS[$real]:-}" ]; then
        return 0
    fi

    base="$(basename -- "$real")"
    case "$base" in *.service|*.timer|*.socket|*.target|*.path|*.mount) : ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
    name="${base%.*}"
    sha="$(file_sha256 "$real")"
    [ -n "$sha" ] || return 0

    local line
    # hidden unit file (starts with '.')

scan_systemd_dir() {
    local dir="$1"
    [ -d "$dir" ] || return 0
    local f
    for f in "$dir"/* "$dir"/.*; do

        case "$f" in */.|*/..) continue ;; esac
        [ -f "$f" ] || continue
        scan_systemd_file "$f"
    done
    return 0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rc.local detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

scan_rc_local() {
    local file="$1"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local sha line lineno
    sha="$(file_sha256 "$file")"
    [ -n "$sha" ] || return 0
    lineno=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))

            "true"|"true"*) continue ;;

}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SSH authorized_keys detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# whitelist of known legitimate keys (one key per line), if it exists
WHITELIST="/app/known_legit_keys.txt"

is_known_legit_key() {
    local key="$1"
    [ -f "$WHITELIST" ] || return 1

    local keytype blob comment

    local rest="${line#* }"
    blob="${rest%% *}"
    comment=""

    if [ -z "$comment" ]; then

    fi
    return 1
}

scan_authorized_keys() {
    local file="$1" user="$2"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local sha line lineno
    sha="$(file_sha256 "$file")"
    [ -n "$sha" ] || return 0
    lineno=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do

        fi

TARGET="/app_target"

done

#
# scan_persistence.sh - Scan a Linux sandbox for post-exploitation persistence
# artifacts (cron jobs, hidden systemd units, rc.local tweaks, rogue SSH keys)
# and emit a structured JSON report at /app/persistence_report.json.
#
# The script is read-only, idempotent, and exits 0 on success.
#
set -u
umask 022

REPORT="/app/persistence_report.json"
TMPDIR_WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR_WORK"' EXIT

ARTIFACTS="$TMPDIR_WORK/artifacts.tsv"
: > "$ARTIFACTS"
# TSV fields: type, path, sha256, line_number, user, preview

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Escape a string for safe inclusion in a JSON string literal.
json_escape() {
    local s="$1"
    s=${s//\\/\\\\}
    s=${s//\"/\\\"}
    s=${s//$'\t'/\\t}
    s=${s//$'\r'/\\r}
    s=${s//$'\n'/\\n}
    # Strip remaining non-printable control characters
    printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037'
}

file_hash() {
    # sha256 of file content (first 64 hex chars); empty string on failure
    local h
    h="$(sha256sum -- "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
    printf '%s' "${h:0:64}"
}

add_artifact() {
    # $1=type $2=path $3=sha256 $4=line_number(or -) $5=user(or -) $6=preview
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" "$6" >> "$ARTIFACTS"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Suspicious-command heuristics (shared by cron / systemd / rc.local)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Obfuscation / remote-access / reverse-shell / download-and-run patterns
SUS_CMD='(base64[[:space:]]+-d|base64[[:space:]]+--decode|\beval\b|\bshred\b|\bchmod[[:space:]]+[0-7]*[67][0-7][0-7]\b|\bmkfifo\b|\bnc\b[[:space:]]|\bncat\b|\bnetcat\b|\bsocat\b|\bssh[[:space:]]+-R\b|bash[[:space:]]+-i|sh[[:space:]]+-i|/dev/tcp/|/dev/udp/|attacker|backdoor|malicious)'
# Network fetchers (curl/wget) - suspicious in persistence contexts
SUS_NET='\bcurl\b|\bwget\b'
# Temp / world-writable directories
SUS_TMP='(/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)'
# Hidden dotfiles in the command
SUS_DOTFILE='(^|[^[:alnum:]_.])\.[^[:space:]/[:space:]]+([^[:space:]]|$)'
# Sensitive locations
SUS_SENS='(/etc/crontab|/etc/cron\.d|/etc/systemd|/etc/rc\.local|/etc/ssh|/var/spool/cron|/etc/passwd|/etc/shadow|/root/\.ssh)'

# Is the command portion (after schedule/user fields) suspicious?
cron_line_suspicious() {

    grep -qE "$SUS_NET" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_TMP" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_DOTFILE" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_SENS" <<<"$line" && return 0

    fi
    if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*\*/[0-9]+[[:space:]]+\*' <<<"$line"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1

# Cron scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# scan_cron_file <file> <with_user_field> <user_override>

    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0

    local actual hash
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"

        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        # skip comments and blank lines

            ''|\#*) continue ;;
        esac
        # skip variable assignments (e.g. SHELL=, PATH=)
        if grep -qE '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' <<<"$line"; then
            continue
        fi
        # must look like a cron schedule (starts with 5 time fields)
        grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+' <<<"$line" || continue

        local user_field=""
        if [ "$with_user" = "1" ]; then
            user_field="$(sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*([^\t]+[[:space:]]+){5}[[:space:]]*//' <<<"$line" | awk '{print $1}')"
        fi
        local user="${user_override:-$user_field}"
        [ -z "$user" ] && user="-"

        if cron_line_suspicious "$line"; then
            local preview
            preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
            add_artifact "cron_job" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "$user" "$preview"
        fi
    done < "$actual"
}

scan_cron() {
    local root="$1"
    # /etc/crontab style (has user field)
    [ -e "$root/etc/crontab" ] && scan_cron_file "$root/etc/crontab" 1 ""
    # /etc/cron.d/* (has user field)
    if [ -d "$root/etc/cron.d" ]; then
        local f
        for f in "$root"/etc/cron.d/* "$root"/etc/cron.d/.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_cron_file "$f" 1 ""
        done
    fi
    # user crontabs in spool (no user field; filename = user)
    if [ -d "$root/var/spool/cron/crontabs" ]; then
        local f
        for f in "$root"/var/spool/cron/crontabs/* "$root"/var/spool/cron/crontabs/.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_cron_file "$f" 0 "$(basename "$f")"
        done
    fi
    # user crontabs in /var/spool/cron/cron.* (Debian layout, no user field)
    if [ -d "$root/var/spool/cron" ]; then
        local f
        for f in "$root"/var/spool/cron/cron.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            scan_cron_file "$f" 0 "$(basename "$f")"
        done
    fi
    # user-specific cron directories
    if [ -d "$root/etc/cron" ]; then
        local f
        for f in "$root"/etc/cron/*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            scan_cron_file "$f" 1 ""
        done
    fi
    # user crontab files under home directories (crontab -e style)
    if [ -d "$root/home" ]; then
        local h f
        for h in "$root"/home/*; do
            [ -d "$h" ] || continue
            f="$h/.crontab"
            [ -f "$f" ] && scan_cron_file "$f" 0 "$(basename "$h")"
        done
    fi
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Systemd unit scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Is a unit file owned by a dpkg package? (only meaningful for /)
dpkg_owned() {
    local f="$1"
    dpkg -S -- "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    local rp
    rp="$(realpath -f -- "$f" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    [ "$rp" = "$f" ] && return 1
    dpkg -S -- "$rp" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

scan_systemd_unit() {
    local file="$1"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local base actual hash
    base="$(basename "$file")"
    case "$base" in
        *.service|*.socket|*.timer|*.target|*.path|*.mount|*.automount|*.swap) : ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac

    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    # skip symlinked-in standard units (e.g. wants/ links to /lib/systemd)
    if [ "$actual" != "$file" ]; then
        # symlink: only flag if target is outside standard systemd dirs
        case "$actual" in
            /usr/lib/systemd/system/*|/lib/systemd/system/*) return 0 ;;
        esac
    fi

    local suspicious=0 reason=""
    # hidden file
    case "$base" in .*) suspicious=1; reason="hidden unit file" ;; esac

    # suspicious ExecStart
    local execline
    execline="$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*ExecStart=' "$actual" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
    if [ -n "$execline" ]; then
        local cmd="${execline#*=}"
        if cron_line_suspicious "$cmd" || grep -qE "$SUS_CMD" <<<"$cmd"; then
            suspicious=1
            [ -z "$reason" ] && reason="suspicious ExecStart"
        fi
    fi

    # not owned by any package (only for real system dirs, not /app_target)
    case "$file" in
        /etc/systemd/system/*|/usr/lib/systemd/system/*|/run/systemd/system/*)
            if [ "$suspicious" = "0" ] && ! dpkg_owned "$file"; then
                # conservative: only flag non-standard names that look
                # like they were planted (avoid flagging every unowned unit)
                case "$base" in
                    *.service)
                        if grep -qE 'ExecStart=' "$actual" 2>/dev/null; then
                            suspicious=1
                            reason="not in standard package database"
                        fi
                        ;;
                esac
            fi
            ;;
    esac

    [ "$suspicious" = "1" ] || return 0

    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0
    local preview
    if [ -n "$execline" ]; then
        preview="$(printf '[Service]\n%s' "${execline#*=}" | cut -c1-100)"
    else
        preview="$(head -n 1 "$actual" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-100)"
    fi
    add_artifact "systemd_unit" "$actual" "$hash" "-" "-" "$preview"
}

scan_systemd() {
    local root="$1"
    local dir f
    for dir in "$root/etc/systemd/system" \
               "$root/usr/lib/systemd/system" \
               "$root/run/systemd/system"; do
        [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
        for f in "$dir"/* "$dir"/.*; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_systemd_unit "$f"
        done
    done
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rc.local scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Standard rc.local content that is NOT considered a modification:
# comments, shebangs, blank lines, "exit 0", and standard init invocations.
rc_local_line_standard() {
    local line="$1"
    case "$line" in
        ''|\#*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*#!' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*exit[[:space:]]*(0)?[[:space:]]*$' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(true|:)[[:space:]]*$' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(/sbin/|/usr/sbin/|/bin/|/usr/bin/)?(rc|service|systemctl|chkconfig|update-rc\.d)' <<<"$line" && return 0
    return 1
}

scan_rc_local() {
    local file="$1"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local actual hash
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    local lineno=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        # strip trailing CR
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        if ! rc_local_line_standard "$line"; then
            local preview
            preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
            add_artifact "rc_local" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "-" "$preview"
        fi
    done < "$actual"
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SSH authorized_keys scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A key is legitimate if it matches a known-good fingerprint (optional
# whitelist at /app/known_authorized_keys) or has a benign comment.
# Without a whitelist, keys with suspicious comments or unknown origins
# are flagged.
LEGIT_COMMENT_RE='(root@|admin@|dev@|ops@|deploy@|ci@|backup@|monitoring@|sysadmin@|server@|host@|laptop@|workstation@|localhost|localhost\.local|\.local$|\.internal$|\.lan$|\.home\.lan|\.corp\.|\.company\.|\.example\.|@localhost|@\.local\b|@\.internal\b)'

key_is_whitelisted() {
    local line="$1"
    [ -f /app/known_authorized_keys ] || return 1
    grep -qxF "$line" /app/known_authorized_keys 2>/dev/null
}

scan_authorized_keys() {
    local file="$1" user="$2"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local actual hash
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    local lineno=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        case "$line" in
            ''|\#*) continue ;;
        esac
        # must be a public key line
        grep -qE '^(ssh-(rsa|dss|ed25519|ed448|ecdsa)|ecdsa-sha2-|sk-ssh-ed25519|sk-ecdsa-sha2-|ssh-rsa-cert|ssh-ed25519-cert|ecdsa-sha2-cert|ssh-dss-cert)' <<<"$line" || continue

        # check whitelist first
        if key_is_whitelisted "$line"; then
            continue
        fi

        local comment=""
        comment="$(awk '{print $NF}')" <<<"$line"
        local suspicious=0
        # suspicious comment heuristics
        if grep -qE '(attacker|backdoor|malicious|unknown|evil|reverse|shell|payload|c2|pwned|hack|root@unknown|@unknown|@attacker|@evil)' <<<"$comment"; then
            suspicious=1
        fi
        # conservative: without a whitelist, flag all keys (they cannot be
        # verified as legitimate); the whitelist file, if present, suppresses
        if [ "$suspicious" = "0" ] && [ ! -f /app/known_authorized_keys ]; then
            # Only flag keys that are clearly not standard local keys:
            # keys without a local-looking comment are treated as unverified.
            if ! grep -qE "$LEGIT_COMMENT_RE" <<<"$comment"; then
                suspicious=1
            fi
        fi
        [ "$suspicious" = "1" ] || continue

        local preview
        preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
        add_artifact "ssh_key" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "$user" "$preview"
    done < "$actual"
    return 0
}

scan_ssh_keys() {
    local root="$1"
    # root's authorized_keys
    [ -e "$root/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" ] && \
        scan_authorized_keys "$root/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" "root"
    # all user home directories
    if [ -d "$root/home" ]; then
        local h
        for h in "$root"/home/*; do
            [ -d "$h" ] || continue
            local f="$h/.ssh/authorized_keys"
            [ -e "$f" ] && scan_authorized_keys "$f" "$(basename "$h")"
        done
    fi
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

scan_rc_local "/etc/rc.local"
scan_rc_local "/etc/rc.d/rc.local"

scan_cron "/"
scan_systemd "/"
scan_ssh_keys "/"

# /app_target is the primary scan location (mirrors a system layout)
if [ -d /app_target ]; then
    scan_rc_local "/app_target/etc/rc.local"
    scan_rc_local "/app_target/etc/rc.d/rc.local"
    scan_cron "/app_target"
    scan_systemd "/app_target"
    scan_ssh_keys "/app_target"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build JSON report
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Sort artifacts: by type, then path, then line number (numeric)
SORTED="$TMPDIR_WORK/sorted.tsv"
LC_ALL=C sort -t$'\t' -k1,1 -k2,2 -k4,4n "$ARTIFACTS" > "$SORTED"

count_type() {
    local t="$1"
    awk -F'\t' -v t="$t" '$1 == t { n++ } END { print n + 0 }' "$SORTED"
}

N_CRON="$(count_type cron_job)"
N_UNIT="$(count_type systemd_unit)"
N_RC="$(count_type rc_local)"
N_SSH="$(count_type ssh_key)"
N_TOTAL=$((N_CRON + N_UNIT + N_RC + N_SSH))

{
    printf '{\n'
    printf '  "summary": {\n'
    printf '    "total_artifacts": %d,\n' "$N_TOTAL"
    printf '    "cron_jobs": %d,\n' "$N_CRON"
    printf '    "systemd_units": %d,\n' "$N_UNIT"
    printf '    "rc_local_modifications": %d,\n' "$N_RC"
    printf '    "ssh_keys": %d\n' "$N_SSH"
    printf '  },\n'
    printf '  "artifacts": ['

    local_first=1
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r atype apath ahash aline auser aprev; do
        [ -n "$atype" ] || continue
        if [ "$local_first" = "1" ]; then
            printf '\n'
            local_first=0
        else
            printf ',\n'
        fi
        printf '    {\n'
        printf '      "type": "%s",\n' "$(json_escape "$atype")"
        printf '      "path": "%s",\n' "$(json_escape "$apath")"
        printf '      "sha256": "%s",\n' "$(json_escape "$ahash")"
        printf '      "details": {\n'
        if [ "$aline" = "-" ] || [ -z "$aline" ]; then
            printf '        "line_number": null,\n'
        else
            printf '        "line_number": %d,\n' "$aline"
        fi
        printf '        "content_preview": "%s",\n' "$(json_escape "$aprev")"
        if [ "$auser" = "-" ] || [ -z "$auser" ]; then
            printf '        "user": null\n'
        else
            printf '        "user": "%s"\n' "$(json_escape "$auser")"
        fi
        printf '      }\n'
        printf '    }'
    done < "$SORTED"

    if [ "$local_first" = "0" ]; then
        printf '\n  '
    fi
    printf ']\n'
    printf '}\n'
} > "$REPORT"

# Validate JSON if a validator is available (non-fatal)
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    python3 -c "import json,sys; json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))" "$REPORT" 2>/dev/null || \
        echo "warning: report failed JSON validation" >&2
fi

exit 0
"}

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# scan_persistence.sh - Scan a Linux sandbox for post-exploitation persistence
# artifacts (malicious cron jobs, hidden systemd units, rc.local tweaks and
# rogue SSH authorized_keys entries) and emit a structured JSON report at
# /app/persistence_report.json.
#
# Properties:
#   * Read-only: never modifies any file it scans.
#   * Idempotent: repeated runs produce byte-identical reports.
#   * Robust: unreadable files / missing directories are skipped gracefully.
#   * Exits 0 on success.
#
set -u
umask 022

REPORT="/app/persistence_report.json"
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

ARTIFACTS="$WORK/artifacts.tsv"
: > "$ARTIFACTS"
# TSV fields: type, path, sha256, line_number(-), user(-), preview

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Escape a string for safe inclusion in a JSON string literal.
json_escape() {
    local s="$1"
    s=${s//\\/\\\\}
    s=${s//\"/\\\"}
    s=${s//$'\t'/\\t}
    s=${s//$'\r'/\\r}
    s=${s//$'\n'/\\n}
    # strip remaining non-printable control characters
    printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037'
}

file_hash() {
    # sha256 of file content (first 64 hex chars); empty on failure
    local h
    h="$(sha256sum -- "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
    printf '%s' "${h:0:64}"
}

add_artifact() {
    # $1=type $2=path $3=sha256 $4=line_number(or -) $5=user(or -) $6=preview
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" "$6" >> "$ARTIFACTS"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Suspicious-command heuristics (shared by cron / systemd / rc.local)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Obfuscation / remote-access / reverse-shell / download-and-run patterns
SUS_CMD='(base64[[:space:]]+(-d|--decode)|\beval\b|\bshred\b|\bchmod[[:space:]]+[0-7]*[67][0-7][0-7]\b|\bmkfifo\b|\bnc\b[[:space:]]|\bncat\b|\bnetcat\b|\bsocat\b|\bssh[[:space:]]+-R\b|bash[[:space:]]+-i|sh[[:space:]]+-i|/dev/tcp/|/dev/udp/|attacker|backdoor|malicious)'
# Network fetchers (curl/wget) - suspicious in persistence contexts
SUS_NET='(^|[[:space:]])(curl|wget)([[:space:]]|$)'
# Temp / world-writable directories
SUS_TMP='(/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)'
# Hidden dotfile referenced in the command
SUS_DOTFILE='(^|[^[:alnum:]_.])\.[^[:space:]/]+([^[:space:]]|$)'
# References to other persistence locations
SUS_SENS='(/etc/crontab|/etc/cron\.d|/etc/systemd|/etc/rc\.local|/etc/ssh|/var/spool/cron|/etc/passwd|/etc/shadow|/root/\.ssh)'

# Absolute paths considered "standard system paths" (not suspicious by
# themselves): /usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib, /opt, /var/lib, /usr/share,
# /etc/cron.* (standard run-parts targets).
is_standard_path() {
    case "$1" in
        /usr/*|/bin/*|/sbin/*|/lib/*|/opt/*|/var/lib/*|/usr/share/*|/etc/cron.*) return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

# Decide whether a command line (cron entry body or ExecStart value) is
# suspicious. Conservative: err on the side of reporting.
line_suspicious() {
    local line="$1"
    grep -qE "$SUS_CMD" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_NET" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_TMP" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_DOTFILE" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_SENS" <<<"$line" && return 0
    # executes a script/binary outside standard system paths
    local p
    while IFS= read -r p; do
        [ -n "$p" ] || continue
        is_standard_path "$p" || return 0
    done < <(grep -oE '(^|[[:space:]])/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)+([[:space:]]|$)' <<<"$line" \
             | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]+//; s/[[:space:]]+$//')
    # unusual timing patterns: every minute or every-N-minutes
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*\*[[:space:]]+\*' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*\*/[0-9]+[[:space:]]+\*' <<<"$line" && return 0
    return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cron scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# scan_cron_file <file> <has_user_field:0|1> <user_override>
scan_cron_file() {
    local file="$1" has_user="$2" user_override="$3"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local actual hash
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    local lineno=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        case "$line" in
            ''|\#*) continue ;;
        esac
        # skip variable assignments (SHELL=, PATH=, ...)
        grep -qE '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' <<<"$line" && continue
        # must start with a 5-field cron schedule
        grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+' <<<"$line" || continue

        local user="$user_override"
        if [ -z "$user" ] && [ "$has_user" = "1" ]; then
            user="$(sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*([^\t]+[[:space:]]+){5}[[:space:]]*//' <<<"$line" | awk '{print $1}')"
        fi
        [ -n "$user" ] || user="-"

        if line_suspicious "$line"; then
            local preview
            preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
            add_artifact "cron_job" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "$user" "$preview"
        fi
    done < "$actual"
    return 0
}

scan_cron() {
    local root="$1" f
    # /etc/crontab (has user field)
    [ -e "$root/etc/crontab" ] && scan_cron_file "$root/etc/crontab" 1 ""
    # /etc/cron.d/* (has user field)
    if [ -d "$root/etc/cron.d" ]; then
        for f in "$root"/etc/cron.d/* "$root"/etc/cron.d/.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_cron_file "$f" 1 ""
        done
    fi
    # user crontabs in spool (no user field; filename = user)
    if [ -d "$root/var/spool/cron/crontabs" ]; then
        for f in "$root"/var/spool/cron/crontabs/* "$root"/var/spool/cron/crontabs/.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_cron_file "$f" 0 "$(basename "$f")"
        done
    fi
    # Debian-style spool files /var/spool/cron/cron.<user>
    if [ -d "$root/var/spool/cron" ]; then
        for f in "$root"/var/spool/cron/cron.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            scan_cron_file "$f" 0 "$(basename "$f")"
        done
    fi
    # user-specific cron directories (e.g. /etc/cron/myjob)
    if [ -d "$root/etc/cron" ]; then
        for f in "$root"/etc/cron/*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            scan_cron_file "$f" 1 ""
        done
    fi
    # user crontab files under home directories
    if [ -d "$root/home" ]; then
        local h
        for h in "$root"/home/*; do
            [ -d "$h" ] || continue
            [ -f "$h/.crontab" ] && scan_cron_file "$h/.crontab" 0 "$(basename "$h")"
        done
    fi
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Systemd unit scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Pre-compute the set of systemd unit paths owned by installed packages
# (single batched dpkg-query call).  Resolved through the /lib symlink.
OWNED_UNITS="$WORK/owned_units"
: > "$OWNED_UNITS"
if command -v dpkg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dpkg -S '/usr/lib/systemd/system/*' '/lib/systemd/system/*' \
               '/etc/systemd/system/*' '/run/systemd/system/*' 2>/dev/null \
        | sed -E 's/^[^:]+:[[:space:]]*//' > "$OWNED_UNITS" || : > "$OWNED_UNITS"
fi

unit_is_package_owned() {
    local f="$1"
    grep -qxF "$f" "$OWNED_UNITS" && return 0
    local rp
    rp="$(realpath -f -- "$f" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    grep -qxF "$rp" "$OWNED_UNITS"
}

scan_systemd_unit() {
    local file="$1"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local base actual
    base="$(basename "$file")"
    case "$base" in
        *.service|*.socket|*.timer|*.target|*.path|*.mount|*.automount|*.swap) : ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac

    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    # Symlinked-in units that point at the standard vendor directory are
    # normal (e.g. wants/ links); only non-standard targets are of interest.
    if [ "$actual" != "$file" ]; then
        case "$actual" in
            /usr/lib/systemd/system/*|/lib/systemd/system/*) return 0 ;;
        esac
    fi

    local suspicious=0
    # 1) hidden unit file (name starts with '.')
    case "$base" in .*) suspicious=1 ;; esac

    # 2) suspicious ExecStart command
    local execline cmd
    execline="$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*ExecStart=' "$actual" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
    if [ -n "$execline" ]; then
        cmd="${execline#*=}"
        # strip leading '-' (systemd "ignore failure" marker)
        cmd="${cmd#-}"
        line_suspicious "$cmd" && suspicious=1
    fi

    # 3) unit not present in any package manifest (system dirs only)
    case "$file" in
        /etc/systemd/system/*|/usr/lib/systemd/system/*|/run/systemd/system/*)

                case "$base" in
                    *.service)

                        # start something (avoid noise from unowned targets)
                        grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*ExecStart=' "$actual" 2>/dev/null && suspicious=1
                        ;;
                esac
            fi
            ;;
    esac

    [ "$suspicious" = "1" ] || return 0

    local hash preview
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0
    if [ -n "$execline" ]; then
        preview="$(printf '%s' "${execline#*=}" | cut -c1-100)"
    else
        preview="$(head -n 1 "$actual" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-100)"
    fi
    add_artifact "systemd_unit" "$actual" "$hash" "-" "-" "$preview"
    return 0
}

scan_systemd() {
    local root="$1" dir f
    for dir in "$root/etc/systemd/system" \
               "$root/usr/lib/systemd/system" \
               "$root/run/systemd/system"; do
        [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
        for f in "$dir"/* "$dir"/.*; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_systemd_unit "$f"
        done
    done
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rc.local scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Lines considered part of standard system initialization (not modifications):
# comments, blank lines, shebangs, "exit 0" / "true" / ":", and standard
# init invocations (rc, service, systemctl, chkconfig, update-rc.d).
rc_local_line_standard() {
    local line="$1"
    case "$line" in
        ''|\#*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*#!' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*exit[[:space:]]*0?[[:space:]]*$' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(true|:)[[:space:]]*$' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(/sbin/|/usr/sbin/|/bin/|/usr/bin/)?(rc|service|systemctl|chkconfig|update-rc\.d)([[:space:]]|$)' <<<"$line" && return 0
    return 1
}

scan_rc_local() {
    local file="$1"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local actual hash
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    local lineno=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        if ! rc_local_line_standard "$line"; then
            local preview
            preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
            add_artifact "rc_local" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "-" "$preview"
        fi
    done < "$actual"
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SSH authorized_keys scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Optional whitelist of known-legitimate key lines: /app/known_authorized_keys
WHITELIST="/app/known_authorized_keys"

# Comments that look like ordinary local/host keys
LEGIT_COMMENT_RE='(root@|admin@|dev@|ops@|deploy@|ci@|backup@|monitoring@|sysadmin@|server@|host@|laptop@|workstation@|localhost|localhost\.local|\.local$|\.local |\.internal$|\.internal |\.lan$|\.lan |\.corp\.|\.company\.|\.example\.)'

key_is_whitelisted() {
    [ -f "$WHITELIST" ] || return 1
    grep -qxF -- "$1" "$WHITELIST" 2>/dev/null
}

scan_authorized_keys() {
    local file="$1" user="$2"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local actual hash
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    local lineno=0 line comment suspicious
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        case "$line" in
            ''|\#*) continue ;;

        if grep -qE '(attacker|backdoor|malicious|unknown|evil|reverse|shell|payload|\bc2\b|pwned|hack)' <<<"$comment"; then
            suspicious=1
        elif [ ! -f "$WHITELIST" ]; then

            # cannot be verified as legitimate -> report them.
            grep -qE "$LEGIT_COMMENT_RE" <<<"$comment" || suspicious=1
        fi
        [ "$suspicious" = "1" ] || continue

        local preview
        preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
        add_artifact "ssh_key" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "$user" "$preview"
    done < "$actual"
    return 0
}

scan_ssh_keys() {
    local root="$1" h f
    [ -e "$root/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" ] && \
        scan_authorized_keys "$root/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" "root"
    if [ -d "$root/home" ]; then

            [ -d "$h" ] || continue
            f="$h/.ssh/authorized_keys"
            [ -e "$f" ] && scan_authorized_keys "$f" "$(basename "$h")"
        done
    fi
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# scan_persistence.sh - Scan a Linux sandbox for post-exploitation persistence
# artifacts (malicious cron jobs, hidden systemd units, rc.local tweaks and
# rogue SSH authorized_keys entries) and emit a structured JSON report at
# /app/persistence_report.json.
#
# Properties:
#   * Read-only: never modifies any file it scans.
#   * Idempotent: repeated runs produce byte-identical reports.
#   * Robust: unreadable files / missing directories are skipped gracefully.
#   * Exits 0 on success.
#
set -u
umask 022

REPORT="/app/persistence_report.json"
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

ARTIFACTS="$WORK/artifacts.tsv"
: > "$ARTIFACTS"
# TSV fields: type, path, sha256, line_number(-), user(-), preview

TAB="$(printf '\t')"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Escape a string for safe inclusion in a JSON string literal.
json_escape() {
    local s="$1"
    s=${s//\\/\\\\}
    s=${s//\"/\\\"}
    s=${s//$'\t'/\\t}
    s=${s//$'\r'/\\r}
    s=${s//$'\n'/\\n}
    # strip remaining non-printable control characters
    printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037'
}

file_hash() {
    # sha256 of file content (first 64 hex chars); empty on failure
    local h
    h="$(sha256sum -- "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
    printf '%s' "${h:0:64}"
}

add_artifact() {
    # $1=type $2=path $3=sha256 $4=line_number(or -) $5=user(or -) $6=preview
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" "$6" >> "$ARTIFACTS"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Suspicious-command heuristics (shared by cron / systemd / rc.local)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Obfuscation / remote-access / reverse-shell / download-and-run patterns
SUS_CMD='(base64[[:space:]]+(-d|--decode)|\beval\b|\bshred\b|\bchmod[[:space:]]+[0-7]*[67][0-7][0-7]\b|\bmkfifo\b|\bnc\b[[:space:]]|\bncat\b|\bnetcat\b|\bsocat\b|\bssh[[:space:]]+-R\b|bash[[:space:]]+-i|sh[[:space:]]+-i|/dev/tcp/|/dev/udp/|attacker|backdoor|malicious)'
# Network fetchers (curl/wget) - suspicious in persistence contexts
SUS_NET='(^|[[:space:]])(curl|wget)([[:space:]]|$)'
# Temp / world-writable directories
SUS_TMP='(/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)'
# Hidden dotfile referenced in the command
SUS_DOTFILE='(^|[^[:alnum:]_.])\.[^[:space:]/]+([^[:space:]]|$)'
# References to other persistence locations
SUS_SENS='(/etc/crontab|/etc/cron\.d|/etc/systemd|/etc/rc\.local|/etc/ssh|/var/spool/cron|/etc/passwd|/etc/shadow|/root/\.ssh)'

# Absolute paths considered "standard system paths" (not suspicious by
# themselves): /usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib, /opt, /var/lib, /usr/share,
# /etc/cron.* (standard run-parts targets).
is_standard_path() {
    case "$1" in
        /usr/*|/bin/*|/sbin/*|/lib/*|/opt/*|/var/lib/*|/usr/share/*|/etc/cron.*) return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

# Decide whether a command line (cron entry body or ExecStart value) is
# suspicious. Conservative: err on the side of reporting.
line_suspicious() {
    local line="$1" p
    grep -qE "$SUS_CMD" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_NET" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_TMP" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_DOTFILE" <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE "$SUS_SENS" <<<"$line" && return 0
    # executes a script/binary outside standard system paths
    while IFS= read -r p; do
        [ -n "$p" ] || continue
        is_standard_path "$p" || return 0
    done < <(grep -oE '(^|[[:space:]])/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)+([[:space:]]|$)' <<<"$line" \
             | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]+//; s/[[:space:]]+$//')
    # unusual timing patterns: every minute or every-N-minutes
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*\*[[:space:]]+\*' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*\*/[0-9]+[[:space:]]+\*' <<<"$line" && return 0
    return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cron scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# scan_cron_file <file> <has_user_field:0|1> <user_override>
scan_cron_file() {
    local file="$1" has_user="$2" user_override="$3"
    local actual hash lineno line user preview
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    lineno=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        case "$line" in
            ''|\#*) continue ;;
        esac
        # skip variable assignments (SHELL=, PATH=, ...)
        grep -qE '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' <<<"$line" && continue
        # must start with a 5-field cron schedule
        grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+[[:space:]]+[\d*/,-]+' <<<"$line" || continue

        user="$user_override"
        if [ -z "$user" ] && [ "$has_user" = "1" ]; then
            user="$(awk '{print $6}')" <<<"$line"
        fi
        [ -n "$user" ] || user="-"

        if line_suspicious "$line"; then
            preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
            add_artifact "cron_job" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "$user" "$preview"
        fi
    done < "$actual"
    return 0
}

scan_cron() {
    local root="$1" f h
    root="${root%/}"
    # /etc/crontab (has user field)
    if [ -e "$root/etc/crontab" ]; then
        scan_cron_file "$root/etc/crontab" 1 ""
    fi
    # /etc/cron.d/* (has user field)
    if [ -d "$root/etc/cron.d" ]; then
        for f in "$root"/etc/cron.d/* "$root"/etc/cron.d/.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_cron_file "$f" 1 ""
        done
    fi
    # user crontabs in spool (no user field; filename = user)
    if [ -d "$root/var/spool/cron/crontabs" ]; then
        for f in "$root"/var/spool/cron/crontabs/* "$root"/var/spool/cron/crontabs/.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_cron_file "$f" 0 "$(basename "$f")"
        done
    fi
    # Debian-style spool files /var/spool/cron/cron.<user>
    if [ -d "$root/var/spool/cron" ]; then
        for f in "$root"/var/spool/cron/cron.*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            scan_cron_file "$f" 0 "$(basename "$f")"
        done
    fi
    # user-specific cron directories (e.g. /etc/cron/myjob)
    if [ -d "$root/etc/cron" ]; then
        for f in "$root"/etc/cron/*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            scan_cron_file "$f" 1 ""
        done
    fi
    # user crontab files under home directories
    if [ -d "$root/home" ]; then
        for h in "$root"/home/*; do
            [ -d "$h" ] || continue
            if [ -f "$h/.crontab" ]; then
                scan_cron_file "$h/.crontab" 0 "$(basename "$h")"
            fi
        done
    fi
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Systemd unit scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Pre-compute the set of systemd unit paths owned by installed packages
# (single batched dpkg-query call).
OWNED_UNITS="$WORK/owned_units"
: > "$OWNED_UNITS"
if command -v dpkg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dpkg -S '/usr/lib/systemd/system/*' '/lib/systemd/system/*' \
               '/etc/systemd/system/*' '/run/systemd/system/*' 2>/dev/null \
        | sed -E 's/^[^:]+:[[:space:]]*//' > "$OWNED_UNITS" || : > "$OWNED_UNITS"
fi

# Is the unit (or its resolved target / /lib<->/usr/lib variant) owned by
# an installed package?
unit_is_package_owned() {
    local f="$1" rp alt
    grep -qxF -- "$f" "$OWNED_UNITS" && return 0
    rp="$(realpath -f -- "$f" 2>/dev/null)" || rp="$f"
    grep -qxF -- "$rp" "$OWNED_UNITS" && return 0
    # /usr/lib may be a symlink to /lib (or vice versa)
    alt="${rp/#\\/usr\\/lib/\\/lib}"
    if [ "$alt" != "$rp" ] && grep -qxF -- "$alt" "$OWNED_UNITS"; then
        return 0
    fi
    alt="${rp/#\\/lib/\\/usr\\/lib}"
    if [ "$alt" != "$rp" ] && grep -qxF -- "$alt" "$OWNED_UNITS"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

scan_systemd_unit() {
    local file="$1"
    local base actual suspicious execline cmd hash preview
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    base="$(basename "$file")"
    case "$base" in
        *.service|*.socket|*.timer|*.target|*.path|*.mount|*.automount|*.swap) : ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac

    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    # Symlinked-in units that point at the standard vendor directory are
    # normal (e.g. wants/ links); only non-standard targets are of interest.
    if [ "$actual" != "$file" ]; then
        case "$actual" in
            /usr/lib/systemd/system/*|/lib/systemd/system/*) return 0 ;;
        esac
    fi

    suspicious=0
    # 1) hidden unit file (name starts with '.')
    case "$base" in .*) suspicious=1 ;; esac

    # 2) suspicious ExecStart command
    execline="$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*ExecStart=' "$actual" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
    if [ -n "$execline" ]; then
        cmd="${execline#*=}"
        # strip systemd prefix markers: '-' (ignore failure), '!' / '!!'
        cmd="$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -E 's/^[!-]+//')"
        if line_suspicious "$cmd"; then
            suspicious=1
        fi
    fi

    # 3) unit not present in any package manifest (system dirs only).
    #    Conservative: only flag unowned units that actually start a program
    #    AND whose ExecStart is not standard (avoids noise from unowned
    #    standard units such as motd-news or rc-local).
    case "$file" in
        /etc/systemd/system/*|/usr/lib/systemd/system/*|/run/systemd/system/*)
            if [ "$suspicious" = "0" ] && ! unit_is_package_owned "$file"; then
                case "$base" in
                    *.service)
                        if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*ExecStart=' "$actual" 2>/dev/null; then
                            suspicious=1
                        fi
                        ;;
                esac
            fi
            ;;
    esac

    [ "$suspicious" = "1" ] || return 0

    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0
    if [ -n "$execline" ]; then
        preview="$(printf '%s' "${execline#*=}" | sed -E 's/^[!-]+//' | cut -c1-100)"
    else

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rc.local scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Lines considered part of standard system initialization (not modifications):
# comments, blank lines, shebangs, "exit 0" / "true" / ":", and standard
# init invocations (rc, service, systemctl, chkconfig, update-rc.d).
rc_local_line_standard() {
    local line="$1"
    case "$line" in
        ''|\#*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*#!' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*exit[[:space:]]*0?[[:space:]]*$' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(true|:)[[:space:]]*$' <<<"$line" && return 0
    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(/sbin/|/usr/sbin/|/bin/|/usr/bin/)?(rc|service|systemctl|chkconfig|update-rc\.d)([[:space:]]|$)' <<<"$line" && return 0
    return 1
}

scan_rc_local() {
    local file="$1"
    local actual hash lineno line preview
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    lineno=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        if ! rc_local_line_standard "$line"; then
            preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
            add_artifact "rc_local" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "-" "$preview"
        fi
    done < "$actual"
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SSH authorized_keys scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Optional whitelist of known-legitimate key lines: /app/known_authorized_keys
WHITELIST="/app/known_authorized_keys"

# Comments that look like ordinary local/host keys
LEGIT_COMMENT_RE='(root@|admin@|dev@|ops@|deploy@|ci@|backup@|monitoring@|sysadmin@|server@|host@|laptop@|workstation@|localhost|localhost\.local|\.local$|\.local |\.internal$|\.internal |\.lan$|\.lan |\.corp\.|\.company\.|\.example\.)'

key_is_whitelisted() {
    [ -f "$WHITELIST" ] || return 1
    grep -qxF -- "$1" "$WHITELIST" 2>/dev/null
}

scan_authorized_keys() {
    local file="$1" user="$2"
    local actual hash lineno line comment suspicious preview
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    actual="$(realpath -f -- "$file" 2>/dev/null)" || actual="$file"
    hash="$(file_hash "$actual")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    lineno=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        case "$line" in
            ''|\#*) continue ;;
        esac
        # must be a public key line
        grep -qE '^(ssh-(rsa|dss|ed25519|ed448|ecdsa)|ecdsa-sha2-|sk-ssh-ed25519|sk-ecdsa-sha2-|ssh-rsa-cert|ssh-ed25519-cert|ecdsa-sha2-cert|ssh-dss-cert)' <<<"$line" || continue

        # whitelisted keys are legitimate
        if key_is_whitelisted "$line"; then
            continue
        fi

        comment="$(awk '{print $NF}')" <<<"$line"
        suspicious=0
        # comments indicating an attacker/backdoor
        if grep -qE '(attacker|backdoor|malicious|unknown|evil|reverse|shell|payload|\bc2\b|pwned|hack)' <<<"$comment"; then
            suspicious=1
        elif [ ! -f "$WHITELIST" ]; then
            # No whitelist: keys without a benign local-looking comment
            # cannot be verified as legitimate -> report them.
            if ! grep -qE "$LEGIT_COMMENT_RE" <<<"$comment"; then
                suspicious=1
            fi
        fi
        if [ "$suspicious" = "1" ]; then
            preview="$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -c1-100)"
            add_artifact "ssh_key" "$actual" "$hash" "$lineno" "$user" "$preview"
        fi
    done < "$actual"
    return 0
}

scan_ssh_keys() {
    local root="$1" h f
    root="${root%/}"
    if [ -e "$root/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" ]; then
        scan_authorized_keys "$root/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" "root"
    fi
    if [ -d "$root/home" ]; then
        for h in "$root"/home/*; do
            [ -d "$h" ] || continue
            f="$h/.ssh/authorized_keys"
            if [ -e "$f" ]; then
                scan_authorized_keys "$f" "$(basename "$h")"
            fi
        done
    fi
    return 0
}

{"path": "/app/scan_persistence.sh", "content": "#!/bin/bash
#
# scan_persistence.sh - Scan a Linux sandbox for post-exploitation
# persistence artifacts and emit a structured JSON report.
#
# Scan locations:
#   - /app_target (primary sandbox location, if it exists)
#   - System persistence locations under / (cron, systemd, rc.local, SSH keys)
#
# Output: /app/persistence_report.json
#
# The script is read-only (never modifies system files) and idempotent.

set -u

REPORT="/app/persistence_report.json"
WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORKDIR"' EXIT

ARTIFACTS="$WORKDIR/artifacts.tsv"
: > "$ARTIFACTS"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# sha256 of a file's content (empty string if unreadable)
file_hash() {
    sha256sum "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | cut -c1-64
}

# Resolve symlinks to the actual file path
resolve_path() {
    realpath -e "$1" 2>/dev/null || readlink -f "$1" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$1"
}

# Extract the command part of a cron line.
# $1 = line, $2 = 1 if the line has a user field (cron.d/crontab), else 0
cron_command() {
    local line="$1" user_field="$2"
    local -a f
    read -r -a f <<< "$line"
    [ "${#f[@]}" -ge 6 ] || return 0
    if [ "$user_field" = "1" ]; then
        printf '%s' "${f[5]}"
    else
        printf '%s' "${f[4]}"
    fi
}

# Check a command string against suspicious patterns.
# Returns 0 (suspicious) or 1 (benign).
# $1 = command text, $2 = 1 if file is owned by a package (benign context)
cmd_suspicious() {
    local cmd="$1" packed="${2:-0}"
    # temporary / world-writable / hidden locations
    case "$cmd" in
        */tmp/*|/tmp/*|*/var/tmp/*|/var/tmp/*|*/dev/shm/*|/dev/shm/*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    # obfuscation / remote payload delivery / reverse shells
    if printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -qE 'base64|eval|sh -c|bash -c|/dev/tcp/'; then
        # plain "sh -c"/"bash -c" wrappers are common in legit cron; only
        # flag when combined with another red flag below, or when unpackaged
        if [ "$packed" = "0" ]; then
            case "$cmd" in
                *curl*|*wget*|*nc*|*/tmp/*|*/var/tmp/*) return 0 ;;
            esac
        fi
    fi
    if printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -qE 'curl|wget'; then return 0; fi
    if printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -qE '(^|[ ;|&(])nc([0-9a-z_-]*)( |$)|ncat'; then return 0; fi
    # pipes into shells
    if printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -qE '\|\s*(ba)?sh($|[ ;])'; then return 0; fi
    # scripts outside standard system paths
    local tok
    for tok in $(printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -oE '(^|[ ;|&](/[^ ;|&]+)+)' | grep -oE '/[^ ;|&]+'); do
        case "$tok" in
            /usr/bin/*|/usr/sbin/*|/bin/*|/sbin/*) : ;;
            /usr/lib/*|/usr/libexec/*|/usr/local/bin/*|/usr/local/sbin/*) : ;;
            /usr/share/*|/usr/local/share/*|/lib/*|/lib64/*) : ;;
            /etc/*|/var/spool/*|/run/*|/proc/*|/sys/*|/dev/*|/opt/*) : ;;
            /app_target/*) return 0 ;;
            *) return 0 ;;
        esac
    done
    return 1
}

# Unusual timing: every minute or short-interval wildcard patterns
cron_timing_suspicious() {
    local sched="$1"
    case "$sched" in
        "* * * * *"|"\*/[0-9] * * * *"|"\*/[0-9] \*/[0-9] * * *"|"\*/[1-9] * * * *") return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cron scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

scan_cron_file() {
    local file="$1" user_field="$2"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local rp; rp="$(resolve_path "$file")"
    [ -f "$rp" ] || return 0
    local hash; hash="$(file_hash "$rp")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    # A file owned by a standard package is treated as a known-good baseline
    local packed=0
    if command -v dpkg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        dpkg -S "$rp" >/dev/null 2>&1 && packed=1
    fi

    local lineno=0 line cmd sched
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        # strip comments / blank lines
        case "$line" in
            ''|\#*) continue ;;
        esac
        # must start with a cron schedule (5 time fields)
        printf '%s' "$line" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(@[a-z_]+|[0-9*,-/]+[[:space:]]+[0-9*,-/]+[[:space:]]+[0-9*,-/]+[[:space:]]+[0-9*,-/]+[[:space:]]+[0-9*,-/]+[[:space:]]+)' || continue

        local -a f
        read -r -a f <<< "$line"
        # @reboot style entries
        if [ "${#f[@]}" -ge 2 ] && [ "${f[0]#@}" != "${f[0]}" ]; then
            if [ "$user_field" = "1" ] && [ "${#f[@]}" -ge 3 ]; then
                cmd="${f[2]}"
            else
                cmd="${f[1]}"
            fi
            local suspicious=1
            if [ "$packed" = "0" ] && cmd_suspicious "$cmd" "$packed"; then
                suspicious=0
            fi
            [ "$suspicious" = "0" ] || continue
        else
            [ "${#f[@]}" -ge 6 ] || continue
            sched="${f[0]} ${f[1]} ${f[2]} ${f[3]} ${f[4]}"
            cmd="$(cron_command "$line" "$user_field")"
            [ -n "$cmd" ] || continue

            local suspicious=1
            if [ "$packed" = "0" ] && cmd_suspicious "$cmd" "$packed"; then
                suspicious=0
            fi
            if [ "$packed" = "0" ] && cron_timing_suspicious "$sched"; then
                suspicious=0
            fi
            [ "$suspicious" = "0" ] || continue
        fi

        local user=null
        if [ "$user_field" = "1" ]; then
            read -r -a f <<< "$line"
            user="${f[5]}"
        fi

        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
            "cron_job" "$rp" "$hash" "$lineno" "$user" >> "$WORKDIR/cron_raw.tsv"
        printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$WORKDIR/preview_${lineno}_${rp//\//_}.txt"
    done < "$rp"
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Systemd unit scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

scan_unit_file() {
    local file="$1"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local rp; rp="$(resolve_path "$file")"
    [ -f "$rp" ] || return 0

    local base; base="$(basename "$rp")"
    case "$base" in
        *.service|*.timer|*.socket|*.target|*.path|*.mount|*.swap) : ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac

    local packed=0
    if command -v dpkg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        dpkg -S "$rp" >/dev/null 2>&1 && packed=1
    fi

    local suspicious=0 reason=""
    # hidden unit files are always suspicious
    case "$base" in
        .*) suspicious=1; reason="hidden unit file" ;;
    esac
    # unpackaged units: flag if ExecStart points outside standard paths or
    # contains remote-fetch / obfuscation patterns
    if [ "$packed" = "0" ]; then
        local execs
        execs="$(grep -hE '^[[:space:]]*ExecStart=' "$rp" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*ExecStart=//; s/^[-+!@]//')"
        if [ -n "$execs" ]; then
            if printf '%s\n' "$execs" | grep -qE '/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/|base64|curl|wget|/dev/tcp/|(^|[ ;|&(])nc([0-9a-z_-]*)( |$)|\|\s*(ba)?sh($|[ ;])'; then
                suspicious=1
                reason="suspicious ExecStart"
            elif printf '%s\n' "$execs" | grep -qE 'sh -c|bash -c'; then
                suspicious=1
                reason="shell-wrapped ExecStart in unpackaged unit"
            else
                # check every absolute path token in ExecStart
                local tok
                for tok in $(printf '%s\n' "$execs" | grep -oE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_=/])/[A-Za-z0-9_./@%-]+'); do
                    case "$tok" in
                        /usr/bin/*|/usr/sbin/*|/bin/*|/sbin/*) : ;;
                        /usr/lib/*|/usr/libexec/*|/usr/local/bin/*|/usr/local/sbin/*) : ;;
                        /usr/share/*|/lib/*|/lib64/*) : ;;
                        /etc/*|/var/*|/run/*|/proc/*|/sys/*|/dev/*|/opt/*) : ;;
                        *) suspicious=1; reason="non-standard ExecStart path"; break ;;
                    esac
                done
            fi
        fi
    fi

    [ "$suspicious" = "1" ] || return 0

    local hash; hash="$(file_hash "$rp")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0
    local preview
    preview="$(grep -hE '^[[:space:]]*ExecStart=' "$rp" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*//')"
    [ -n "$preview" ] || preview="$base: $reason"
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "systemd_unit" "$rp" "$hash" "null" "null" >> "$WORKDIR/cron_raw.tsv"
    printf '%s\n' "$preview" >> "$WORKDIR/preview_unit_${rp//\//_}.txt"
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rc.local scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

scan_rclocal() {
    local file="$1"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local rp; rp="$(resolve_path "$file")"
    [ -f "$rp" ] || return 0

    local hash; hash="$(file_hash "$rp")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    local lineno=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        # trim
        local t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        case "$t" in
            ''|\#*) continue ;;
        esac
        # standard boilerplate
        case "$t" in
            '#!'*) continue ;;
            'exit'*) continue ;;
            'true') continue ;;
            'echo'*) continue ;;
        esac
        # anything else is an unauthorized addition
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
            "rc_local" "$rp" "$hash" "$lineno" "null" >> "$WORKDIR/cron_raw.tsv"
        printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$WORKDIR/preview_rc_${lineno}_${rp//\//_}.txt"
    done < "$rp"
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SSH authorized_keys scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Whitelist of known-legitimate public keys (empty by default).
WHITELIST_FILE="/app/known_legit_keys.txt"
if [ ! -f "$WHITELIST_FILE" ]; then
    WHITELIST_FILE=""
fi

key_is_whitelisted() {
    [ -n "$WHITELIST_FILE" ] || return 1
    grep -qF "$1" "$WHITELIST_FILE" 2>/dev/null
}

scan_authorized_keys() {
    local file="$1" user="$2"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    [ -r "$file" ] || return 0
    local rp; rp="$(resolve_path "$file")"
    [ -f "$rp" ] || return 0

    local hash; hash="$(file_hash "$rp")"
    [ -n "$hash" ] || return 0

    local lineno=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        lineno=$((lineno + 1))
        local t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        case "$t" in
            ''|\#*) continue ;;
        esac
        # must look like a public key
        case "$t" in
            ssh-*|ecdsa-*|sk-ssh-*|sk-ecdsa-*|ssh-ed25519*|ssh-rsa*|ssh-dss*) : ;;
            *) continue ;;
        esac
        # skip whitelisted keys
        if key_is_whitelisted "$t"; then
            continue
        fi
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
            "ssh_key" "$rp" "$hash" "$lineno" "$user" >> "$WORKDIR/cron_raw.tsv"
        printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$WORKDIR/preview_ssh_${lineno}_${rp//\//_}.txt"
    done < "$rp"
    return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run scans
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

scan_all() {
    local base="$1"

    # --- cron ---
    [ -d "$base/etc/cron.d" ] && {
        local f
        for f in "$base"/etc/cron.d/*; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            scan_cron_file "$f" 1
        done
    }
    [ -f "$base/etc/crontab" ] && scan_cron_file "$base/etc/crontab" 1
    [ -d "$base/var/spool/cron/crontabs" ] && {
        local f
        for f in "$base"/var/spool/cron/crontabs/*; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            scan_cron_file "$f" 0
        done
    }
    [ -d "$base/var/spool/cron/crontabs" ] && {
        local f
        for f in "$base"/var/spool/cron/crontabs/.*; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$f")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
            scan_cron_file "$f" 0
        done
    }
    # user-specific cron directories (var/spool/cron/crontabs already covered;
    # also scan /etc/cron.{hourly,daily,weekly,monthly} for suspicious scripts)
    local d f
    for d in "$base"/etc/cron.hourly "$base"/etc/cron.daily "$base"/etc/cron.weekly "$base"/etc/cron.monthly; do
        [ -d "$d" ] || continue
        for f in "$d"/*; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            local rp; rp="$(resolve_path "$f")"
            [ -f "$rp" ] || continue
            # flag scripts in these dirs that are unpackaged and suspicious
            local packed=0
            command -v dpkg >/dev/null 2>&1 && dpkg -S "$rp" >/dev/null 2>&1 && packed=1
            [ "$packed" = "1" ] && continue
            local hash; hash="$(file_hash "$rp")"
            [ -n "$hash" ] || continue
            # read first executable line as preview
            local preview
            preview="$(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$rp" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
            [ -n "$preview" ] || preview="$(head -1 "$rp" 2>/dev/null)"
            printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
                "cron_job" "$rp" "$hash" "null" "null" >> "$WORKDIR/cron_raw.tsv"
            printf '%s\n' "$preview" >> "$WORKDIR/preview_cronscript_${rp//\//_}.txt"
        done
    done

    # --- systemd ---
    local u
    for u in "$base"/etc/systemd/system/*; do
        [ -e "$u" ] || continue
        case "$(basename "$u")" in
            *.service|*.timer|*.socket|*.path|*.mount|*.swap) scan_unit_file "$u" ;;
        esac
    done
    for u in "$base"/etc/systemd/system/.*; do
        [ -e "$u" ] || continue
        case "$(basename "$u")" in .|..) continue ;; esac
        scan_unit_file "$u"
    done
    for u in "$base"/usr/lib/systemd/system/*; do
        [ -e "$u" ] || continue
        case "$(basename "$u")" in
            *.service|*.timer|*.socket|*.path|*.mount|*.swap) scan_unit_file "$u" ;;
        esac
    done
    [ -d "$base/run/systemd/system" ] && {
        for u in "$base"/run/systemd/system/*; do
            [ -e "$u" ] || continue
            case "$(basename "$u")" in
                *.service|*.timer|*.socket|*.path|*.mount|*.swap) scan_unit_file "$u" ;;
            esac
        done
    }

    # --- rc.local ---
    scan_rclocal "$base/etc/rc.local"
    scan_rclocal "$base/etc/rc.d/rc.local"

    # --- SSH authorized_keys ---
    local h
    for h in "$base"/home/*; do
        [ -d "$h" ] || continue
        local uname; uname="$(basename "$h")"
        scan_authorized_keys "$h/.ssh/authorized_keys" "$uname"
    done
    scan_authorized_keys "$base/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" "root"
}

# Primary scan location first, then the container root.
[ -d /app_target ] && scan_all /app_target
scan_all /

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build JSON report
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

RAW="$WORKDIR/cron_raw.tsv"

# Sort by type, then path (and line number for stable ordering)
sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k1,1 -k2,2 -k4,4n "$RAW" > "$WORKDIR/sorted.tsv" 2>/dev/null \
    || sort "$RAW" > "$WORKDIR/sorted.tsv"

{
    printf '{\n  "summary": {\n'
    total=0; ncron=0; nsd=0; nrc=0; nssh=0
    while IFS="$(printf '\t')" read -r type path hash lineno user; do
        [ -n "$type" ] || continue
        total=$((total + 1))
        case "$type" in
            cron_job) ncron=$((ncron + 1)) ;;
            systemd_unit) nsd=$((nsd + 1)) ;;
            rc_local) nrc=$((nrc + 1)) ;;
            ssh_key) nssh=$((nssh + 1)) ;;
        esac

# sha256 of a file's content (empty string if unreadable)
file_hash() {

}

# Resolve symlinks to the actual file path

cmd_suspicious() {

{"command": "cd /app && mkdir -p output && cat > solve.py <<'EOF'
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, json, os
os.makedirs('output', exist_ok=True)
imp = pd.read_csv('data/impressions.csv')
conv = pd.read_csv('data/conversions.csv')
tc = pd.read_csv('data/test_contexts.csv')
m = imp.merge(conv, on='impression_id', how='left')
m['c'] = (m.conversion_value.fillna(0)>0).astype(int)
m['v'] = m.conversion_value.fillna(0)

# ---------- Task 1: delay model (lognormal MLE) ----------
d = conv.delay_hours.values
ln = np.log(d)
mu, sigma = ln.mean(), ln.std(ddof=0)
from scipy.stats import norm
p90 = np.exp(mu + sigma*norm.ppf(0.90))

# ---------- delay correction ----------
# P(convert | age) = 1 - S(age); pending mass = S(age)
# S(age) = P(D > age) * P(convert)  (delay truncated at 72h)
T = 72.0
def S_of_age(age):
    z1 = (np.log(max(age,1e-9)) - mu)/sigma
    z2 = (np.log(T) - mu)/sigma
    cdf = norm.cdf
    F = cdf(z1) if age < T else 1.0
    return (1.0 - F)/cdf(z2)
age = (m.timestamp.max() - m.timestamp)/3600.0
S = np.array([S_of_age(a) for a in age])
# corrected counts: obs + S*rate (iterate to fixed point)
rate = m.c.mean()
for _ in range(10):
    E = m.c + S*rate
    rate = E.sum()/len(m)
print("corrected overall rate:", rate, "obs:", m.c.mean())

# ---------- arm stats ----------
arm_stats = []
arm_rate, arm_val = {}, {}
for a, g in m.groupby('arm_id'):
    n = len(g); k = int(g.c.sum())
    E_a = g.c + S[g.index]*rate  # expected conversions given delay
    r_a = E_a.sum()/n
    v_a = g.v[g.c>0].mean()
    arm_rate[a] = r_a; arm_val[a] = v_a
    arm_stats.append(dict(arm_id=a, estimated_conversion_rate=r_a,
                          estimated_avg_value=v_a, total_impressions=n,
                          total_conversions=k))
pd.DataFrame(arm_stats).to_csv('output/arm_statistics.csv', index=False)

# ---------- contextual multipliers (multiplicative model) ----------
ov = m.c.mean()
hour_m = (m.groupby('hour_of_day')['c'].mean()/ov).reindex(range(24)).values
day_m = (m.groupby('day_of_week')['c'].mean()/ov).reindex(range(7)).values
seg_m = (m.groupby('user_segment')['c'].mean()/ov).to_dict()
dev_m = (m.groupby('device_type')['c'].mean()/ov).to_dict()
# arm x hour relative multiplier (smoothed with global arm rate)
g = m.groupby(['hour_of_day','arm_id'])['c'].agg(['sum','count']).reset_index()
g['r'] = g['sum']/g['count']
g['rate_rel'] = g['r']/g['arm_id'].map(arm_rate)
# shrink toward 1: weight = n_a
n_a = m.groupby('arm_id')['c'].count().to_dict()
g['w'] = g['count'].map(lambda c: c/(c+30))
g['rate_rel_sm'] = 1 + (g['rate_rel']-1)*g['w']
rel = g.pivot(index='hour_of_day', columns='arm_id', values='rate_rel_sm').reindex(range(24)).fillna(1.0)
# arm x day relative
g2 = m.groupby(['day_of_week','arm_id'])['c'].agg(['sum','count']).reset_index()
g2['r'] = g2['sum']/g2['count']; g2['rate_rel'] = g2['r']/g2['arm_id'].map(arm_rate)
g2['w'] = g2['count'].map(lambda c: c/(c+30)); g2['rate_rel_sm'] = 1+(g2['rate_rel']-1)*g2['w']
reld = g2.pivot(index='day_of_week', columns='arm_id', values='rate_rel_sm').reindex(range(7)).fillna(1.0)

# ---------- predictions ----------
arms = np.arange(10)
rows = []
for _, t in tc.iterrows():
    h, dw = t.hour_of_day, t.day_of_week
    ctx = hour_m[h]*day_m[dw]*seg_m[t.user_segment]*dev_m[t.device_type]
    rates = arm_rate[np.arange(10)]*rel.loc[h].values*reld.loc[dw].values
    probs = np.clip(rates*ctx, 0, 1)
    vals = np.array([arm_val[a] for a in arms])
    er = probs*vals
    best = int(np.argmax(er))
    p, v = er[best], vals[best]
    # 80% CI via delta method on log scale of rate (value treated as known)
    n_a = n_a[best]
    se_log = np.sqrt(1/n_a + 1/200)  # plus shrinkage uncertainty
    lo = max(0.0, p*np.exp(-1.2816*se_log))*v
    hi = p*np.exp(1.2816*se_log)*v
    rows.append((t.context_id, best, er[best], lo, hi))
pred = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['context_id','selected_arm','expected_reward','confidence_lower','confidence_upper'])
pred.to_csv('output/predictions.csv', index=False)

json.dump(dict(distribution_type='lognormal',
               parameters=dict(mu=float(mu), sigma=float(sigma)),
               median_delay_hours=float(np.exp(mu)),
               p90_delay_hours=float(p90),
               conversion_rate_estimate=float(rate)),
          open('output/delay_model.json','w'), indent=2)
print(pred.selected_arm.value_counts().sort_index().to_string())
print("mean ER:", pred.expected_reward.mean(), "mean CI width:", (pred.confidence_upper-pred.confidence_lower).mean())
print("delay model:", json.dumps(dict(mu=mu, sigma=sigma, med=np.exp(mu), p90=p90, rate=rate)))
EOF

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, json
from scipy.stats import norm

imp = pd.read_csv('data/impressions.csv')
conv = pd.read_csv('data/conversions.csv')
test = pd.read_csv('data/test_contexts.csv')
end = imp.timestamp.max()

# ---------- Task 1: Delay model (lognormal MLE) ----------
d = conv.delay_hours.values
ln = np.log(d)
mu = ln.mean()
sigma = ln.std(ddof=0)
median = np.exp(mu)
p90 = np.exp(mu + norm.ppf(0.90)*sigma)

# conversion_rate_estimate: delay-corrected overall rate.
# Use impressions with complete 72h window + expected pending for incomplete ones.
# Simpler robust estimate: rate on complete window (last 72h excluded)
comp_mask = (end - imp.timestamp) >= 72*3600
comp = imp[comp_mask].copy()
comp['y'] = comp.impression_id.isin(conv.impression_id).astype(int)
rate_complete = comp.y.mean()
# pending correction for incomplete impressions
incomp = imp[~comp_mask].copy()
incomp['y'] = incomp.impression_id.isin(conv.impression_id).astype(int)
# fraction of conversions expected to have arrived by data end, given delay cdf
F = lambda x: norm.cdf((np.log(np.clip(x,1e-9,None)) - mu)/sigma)
# age of each incomplete impression at data end
age = (end - incomp.timestamp)/3600.0
expected_rate_incomp = (incomp.y.sum() + (len(incomp)-incomp.y.sum())*F(age).mean()) / len(incomp)
n_tot = len(imp); c_tot = imp.impression_id.isin(conv.impression_id).sum() + (len(incomp)-incomp.y.sum())*F(age).mean()
rate_corrected = c_tot / n_tot
print("rate complete:", rate_complete, "rate corrected:", rate_corrected)

delay_model = {
    "distribution_type": "lognormal",
    "parameters": {"mu": float(mu), "sigma": float(sigma)},
    "median_delay_hours": float(median),
    "p90_delay_hours": float(p90),
    "conversion_rate_estimate": float(rate_complete),
}
with open('output/delay_model.json','w') as f:
    json.dump(delay_model, f, indent=2)

# ---------- Task 2/3: Contextual policy ----------
# Build training set: complete impressions with labels, plus value info
comp_full = comp.merge(conv[['impression_id','conversion_value']], on='impression_id', how='left')
